I went back to the spot where I had lost the key the other night, and
saw that the big building was still standing where it fell down before
me in the grey dusk, a huge white ghost with a red cross on its breast.
In the twilight there was something very touching in this senseless
structure: it was like some giant’s ruin. There was a kind of wild,
patriotic romance in the idea of a building which had failed at last;
like a fortress fallen at last to the enemy. In my heart, I know, was
the same wild patriotism which made the soldiers shout “Huzza for
England” while they were falling in heaps by the roadside. For the
thing is this: we are fighting for things which seem to be losing the
fight. It has never been more clear than at this moment that this
world is going to hell; but it is also quite plain that we are trying
to save heaven. To see a thing thus standing like an ill-built
castle, the last of its dynasty, with its broken towers and its
broken battlements, is almost like being shot through the body. And the
more you look at the thing, the more you can see what is wrong with it.
The main thing seems to be that it has too many stories; that its
architecture is out of date. This is one of those ages when the world
is turning upside down. Men have grown too tall; too tall for the old
buildings. The towers tower up to heaven.
